title: Queso Wars: Texas vs Arkansas
description: Two states, one melty feud, and a Capitol Hill showdown—five steps into cheese-dip lore.

questions.question: Texas and Arkansas feud over who invented what party dip?
questions.explanation: Arkansas champions "cheese dip"; Texas claims chile con queso as its own Tex-Mex birthright—the rivalry is cultural, not just culinary.

questions.question: In the cheese dip feud, which state's senator challenged Texas to a blind Capitol taste test in December 2016?
questions.explanation: Senator Tom Cotton picked the Twitter fight; Texas's Cruz and Cornyn accepted. On Dec. 7, 2016, Republican senators voted blind—and Arkansas won. Cotton missed it: his wife was in labor.

questions.question: Arkansas's cheese-dip origin story centers on Mexico Chiquito, a 1935 dirt-floor restaurant in what city?
questions.explanation: Blackie Donnally and his wife came up from Texas and opened Mexico Chiquito in North Little Rock's Prothro Junction (some accounts start it briefly in Hot Springs). The irony: Arkansas's dip has Texan roots.

questions.question: Texas tailgaters answer North Little Rock's claim by pairing Velveeta with what canned tomato-chile brand?
questions.explanation: Carl Roettele created Rotel in Elsa, Texas, in 1943—the brand became inseparable from tailgates and living-room crock pots on the Texas side of the feud.

questions.question: Rotel was first canned in Elsa in what year?
questions.explanation: That year locks the Texas side of the story: a border-state canning innovation later married to Velveeta in countless home recipes.
